newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unions says reached printing wages deal.
newsitem.headline: German unions says reached printing wages deal.

text.p: Germany's printing union IG Medien said on Thursday it had achieved a concrete result in its wage talks with employers for the industry's 130,000 workers after a marathon negotiating session.
"We have a result," IG Medien negotiator Franz Kersjes told reporters, but declined to give further details.

Earlier, Kersjes had said negotiators were close to a deal that would offer a wage increase as well as lay out concrete rules for sick-pay benefits which are allowed to be changed under a law passed by Bonn late last year.

Industry employers have said wages were likely to rise about 1.5 percent under the deal to take effect on April 1. Sick-pay benefits would be maintained at 100 percent but the annual Christmas bonus would be cut by five percent.
